text:
Stone, too, takes flight when stars are out.
Over the cold, beveled night,
grow, twin lilies of daring;
grow, surge, towers of Compostela.


Your brow longs for a field of stars,
silent mistresses of persistence.
In my breast—oh, love—my fantasy
builds higher towers. The soul keeps vigil.


And she—you—here with me, though your fingers
cannot reach my towers of hope
as mine can touch these stone ones,


look through my towers at the stars,
not these of autumn—erase them; those
of our August burning in cold dreams.

translation.title: Before the Towers of Compostela
